2. The relevant facts briefly are that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No. 200 of 2000 in the Court of the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Chapainawabgonj against the defendant opposite parties for permanent injunction. The plaintiff's case in short is that the owner of the suit land as described in the "Ka" and "Kha" schedule of the plaint was the Government; that during the SA survey those scheduled properties were listed as khas land in the khatian No. 1 and during the RS survey those properties were also listed as Government's khas land but a disputed portion of dag No. 293 was wrongly recorded in the name of some other persons; that one Md Ismail Hossain and Md Saifuddin Mollah, the father of the plaintiff-petitioner were landless and that they applied to the Government for permanent settlement of the land and the Government granted the permanent settlement of the Plot No. 1 as described in schedule No. "Ka" to Md Ismail Hossain and another portion of land as described in schedule "Kha" through permanent Settlement Case No. 202/IX-11/76-77 for 15 years starting from the date of 1" Baisak 1384 to 30th Chaitro 1398 through the permanent settlement registered Kabiliat No. 12734/78 dated 31-7-1978; that the father of the plaintiff-petitioner Md Saifuddin Mollah also executed the registered Kabiliat No. 12731/78 dated 31-7-1978 granted by the Government as permanent settlement for 15 years from the date of 1 Baisak, 1384 to 30th Chaitra, 1398 through permanent settlement Case No. 214/IX-11/76-77; that since then the petitioner's father paid the rents and continued his possession over the disputed land. In this background they said Md Ismail Hossain went to the tahsilder office on 25-8-1982 for paying the rent and for first time he came to know about the fact that RS Dag No 293 was recorded in the Khatian pursuance of former Dag No. 457 and RS Dag No. 293 is opened in RS 205 Khatian in the name of one Md Anisur Rahman wrongly and incorrectly; Thereupon, plaintiff's father Md Saifuddin Mollah filed the Other Class Suit No. 876/83 in the Court of learned Munssif, Chapai Nawabganj against the, opposite parties; that Md Ismail Hossain also filed the Other Class Suit No. 472of 83 in the Court of learned Munsif, Chapai Nawabganj against the opposite parties and Government of Bangladesh for the recovery of 0,84 acres of land recorded in RS Khatian Dag No 293 arising out of former Dag No. 457; that the opposite parties did not appear and contest those two suits and thereupon, the learned Court of Munsif passsed ex-party decrees in favor of the petitioner's father and Md Ismail Hossain. Thereafter, the father of the petitioner and Md Ismail Hossain continued their possessions over the land granted as permanent settlement by the Government of Bangladesh and paid rents regularly; that Md Saifuddin Mollah, the father of the petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 5/X-II1/93-94 to the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Chapai Nawabganj for correction of the Record-of-Rights; that the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), ChapaiNawabganj passed an order in pursuance of the Miscellaneous Case No. 38/X-111/94-95 for correction of the RS Khatian; that thereafter Md Saifuddin Mollah, the father of the petitioner transferred the disputed 0.50 acres of land recorded in RS 293 dag arising out of former dag No 457 by a registered Heba-bil-Awaj deed No. 14934/93 dated 14-10-1997; that Md Ismail Hossain also transferred the rest 0.84 acres of land of RS 293 dag arising out of former dag No.457 to the plaintiff-petitioner by registered sale deed No. 9755 dated 20-6-1993; that the plaintiff-petitioner also continued his possession over that. total 134 acres of land in RS Dag No. 293 but wrongly and incorrectly the quantity of land is recorded as 2.09 acres; that the petitioner and his father continued their possession over the total 1.34 acres of land since the permanent settlement was granted in the year of 1977-78; that on 15-9-2000 the defendant opposite parties tried to dispossess the plaintiff petitioner and threatened to cut the crops produced on the disputed land, the defendant opposite parties also threatened to the plaintiff-petitioner saying to sale the disputed land at taka 20,000 otherwise they will take all produced crops of the property. The defendant opposite parties also threatened to dispossess the petitioner from the disputed land and hence, the suit. 

 10. Mr Md Abdullahel Baki, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-opposite party, on the other hand, opposes the Rule and supports the impugned judgment and decree, which was according to him just, correct and proper. The learned Advocate submits that the property as related in the decrees passed in Other Class Suit No. 476 of 1983 and 479 of 1983 are not at all related with the property of the present suit and therefore, the said decrees cannot stand in the way of well-founded judgment of the Court of appeal below. The learned Advocate further submits that in this case the plaintiff could not adduce any specific or clear evidence as to their possession in the suit land. Besides, the suit land as described in the schedule of the plaint is totally and thoroughly unspecified. Besides, in the facts and circumstances of the case the instant suit for permanent injunction is not maintainable as the property in question is an ancestral property of the defendants. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiff has not taken any attempt towards proving their title or possession in the suit land, plaintiff has neither exhibited CS khatian nor the kabuliyat of permanent settlement No. 12731/78 and 13734/78, the PW I admitted that “কবুলিয়ত নামাগুলো দাখিল করি নাই।” As such, the plaintiff -petitioner has miserably failed to prove their title and possession. He adds that the remedy in a suit for permanent injunction being an equitable one and that the plaintiff must come with clean hands, here the plaintiff's vendors, very tactfully, filed Other Class Suit No, 476/83 and 479/83 praying for declaration of title in shabek plot No. 457 and after obtaining ex-parte decree amended the schedule and entered the schedule of the defendant's property without notifying the defendants, the plaintiff being out of possession filed this suit for permanent injunction as a test case to enter into possession of the suit land and, as such, the plaintiff has not come with clean hands and hence is not entitled to get an equitable relief, as prayed for.
